title: Political opinion: arrests after a march

exchanges.q: Please state your full name for the record.
Where were you living before you came to the United States?
exchanges.a: I lived in {CITY}, with my wife and our two daughters.

exchanges.q: What organization did you belong to?
exchanges.a: I was a member of the {PARTY}. I joined in 2016, and I organized meetings in my neighborhood.

exchanges.q: What happened on the day of the march?
a: On the twelfth of March 2021, we marched to the city hall. The police arrived around noon.
They arrested me and my brother {BROTHER}. They held us for three days without food.

exchanges.q: How many times were you arrested in total?
exchanges.a: Three times. The second time was in June 2021, and the third time was in January 2022.

exchanges.q: What happened during the third arrest?
a: Two officers took me to the station at night. They beat me with sticks and told me they would kill me if I kept organizing.
I think there were five or six other prisoners there, but I am not sure.

exchanges.q: Did you report any of these arrests to anyone?
exchanges.a: No. I did not report them, because the people who arrested me were the police.

exchanges.q: Did anyone in your family receive threats after you left?
exchanges.a: Yes. My wife received two letters at our house. One said that they were looking for me.
I left on the fifth of February 2022, about two weeks after the third arrest.

exchanges.q: Why do you believe they would harm you if you return?
exchanges.a: Because they know my name and my face. My brother is still in hiding, and they came to my mother's house last year.
